summary:
Hopscotch is a children’s game played worldwide on a numbered course drawn on the ground. Players toss a small marker into each square in sequence, then hop through the course while skipping the square containing it. Single squares are usually hopped on one foot, while paired squares are straddled. Players turn at a home or safe space, return to retrieve the marker, and continue. Stepping on a line, missing a square, or losing balance ends a turn; the first to complete every numbered square wins.

Course designs and rules vary. The game has different names around the world, including rayuela in Spanish-speaking regions, marelle in France, piko in the Philippines, and engklek in Indonesia. Some variations add rules such as claiming squares.

Hopscotch’s origin is unknown. Claims that it was played in ancient times lack evidence, and the earliest known English-language references date to the late 17th century, when it was called “scotch-hop” or “scotch-hoppers.” The name combines “hop” with “scotch,” meaning a line or scratch.
